content.title: Recommendations (ACS / ECG)
content.overview: Base diagnosis and initial short-term risk stratification of ACS on clinical history, symptoms, vital signs, other physical findings, ECG, and hs-cTn.

ecg_recommendations.text: Twelve-lead ECG recording and interpretation is recommended as soon as possible at the point of first medical contact (FMC), with a target of <10 minutes.

Continuous ECG monitoring and availability of defibrillator capacity is recommended as soon as possible in all patients with suspected STEMI, in suspected ACS with other ECG changes or ongoing chest pain, and once the diagnosis of MI is made.
Use of additional ECG leads (V3R, V4R, and V7–V9) is recommended in cases of inferior STEMI or if total vessel occlusion is suspected and standard leads are inconclusive.
An additional 12-lead ECG is recommended in cases with recurrent symptoms or diagnostic uncertainty.
